title: Upward Flux Through a Paraboloid Cap
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Compute the upward flux of F = <0, 0, z> through the paraboloid z = 4 - x^2 - y^2 for z >= 0.

steps.title: Apply Upward Normal Flux Formula
steps.mathExpression: z = f(x, y) = 4 - x^2 - y^2 \implies \mathbf{n}\,d\sigma = \langle 2x, 2y, 1 \rangle \, dA
steps.explanation: The upward normal vector for z = f(x, y) is <-f_x, -f_y, 1>.

steps.title: Evaluate Dot Product F . n d sigma
steps.mathExpression: \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n}\,d\sigma = [0(2x) + 0(2y) + z(1)] \, dA = z \, dA = (4 - x^2 - y^2) \, dA
steps.explanation: Take inner product of F and normal element.

steps.title: Integrate in Polar Coordinates
steps.explanation: Evaluate polar integral over base circle of radius 2.
